title: NUMA-aware token-priority IO-fusion prefill scheduler
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Reduce host-side overhead during prefill and decode by combining a NUMA-aware staging arena, per-request token-priority IO fusion, and a lightweight scheduling shim that exposes kernel-selection hints to the GPU dispatcher. Goal is to cut median host CPU cycles per request by ~35% on multi-socket machines and reduce tail latency from threadpool contention and unnecessary memcpy amplification.

Background: Recently we observed sustained host CPU spikes and increased p99 prefill latency on 2-socket instances when under mixed short and long request workloads. Investigation showed three contributing factors: (1) cross-NUMA memory copies for staging pinned pages, (2) scatter/gather memcpy fanout for many small prefill batches, and (3) threadpool thrashing when long-running decode requests block prefill workers. Existing tickets targeted coalescing and prefetching but lacked a combined NUMA and priority-aware approach that ties into kernel selection.

Proposal: Implement a three-part runtime enhancement: 
1) NUMA-aware staging arenas: allocate per-socket pinned buffer pools and preferentially place per-request KV/prefix staging on the local socket. Fall back to inter-socket placement only when local pool is exhausted. Expose a runtime metric for pool pressure.
2) Token-priority IO fusion: classify requests at ingress into priority buckets based on remaining tokens and latency SLO (e.g., short interactive vs long batch). For small/interactive requests, perform in-place append fusion to reduce the number of separate host->GPU memcpy operations. For long requests, group operations into coalesced scatter-gather windows to amortize kernel dispatch overhead.
3) Kernel-hint scheduler shim: at prefill time, emit a lightweight hint describing token distribution (short/long), attention window expectations, and whether quantized kernels are acceptable. The GPU kernel selector can use this to choose lower-latency kernels or bundled dispatch paths. This shim is intentionally non-blocking and only advisory to preserve safety.

Design details: 
- Memory: implement per-NUMA slab allocators with configurable slab size and watermark thresholds. Slabs use pinned pages and are exposed through a small allocation API: allocate_local_or_remote(token_estimate, size_hint). Metrics: slab_hits, slab_fallbacks, slab_evictions.
- Scheduling: augment the host prefill queue with a two-tier queue: high-priority short-token queue (fast-path, single memcpy when possible) and bulk queue (coalescing windows). A token estimator at enqueue time tags the request; tags can be adjusted at runtime as the request is prefetched.
- IO fusion: use single contiguous staging regions for short requests and an indexed scatter table for bulk requests. Implement a micro-batcher that triggers either on count or byte thresholds.
- Kernel hints: add a compact hint structure (flags as bitmask string in scheduler metadata) that surface to the kernel router: acceptable_quantized=1, prefer_low_latency=1, expected_prefix_len=12, expected_decode_len=16. Hints are advisory; kernel selector falls back gracefully.

Implementation plan & milestones: 
- Week 1 (Spike, 3d): prototype NUMA slab allocator and benchmark allocation latency vs current allocator on 2-socket c6gn-like instance.
- Week 2 (Design + PR, 5d): implement per-socket staging arenas and integrate allocation API into prefill path. Add metrics and a feature flag.
- Week 3 (IO fusion, 5d): implement token-priority classification and micro-batcher for short-path fusion. Add unit tests and microbench harness.
- Week 4 (Kernel hinting + integration, 7d): emit kernel hints from scheduler and adapt kernel router to consume hints for kernel selection; keep backward compatible path.
- Week 5 (End-to-end testing + perf runs, 5d): run mixed workload perf tests, collect p50/p95/p99 for CPU cycles and prefill latency, measure memcpy counts per request.
- Week 6 (Rollout, 3d): enable by default behind runtime-1.20 feature gate if metrics meet targets, monitor metrics for regressions.

Testing & acceptance criteria: 
- Unit and integration tests for allocator correctness and fallback behavior.
- Microbench: achieve >=35% reduction in host CPU cycles per short interactive request on 2-socket baseline in controlled harness.
- Production canary: pilot on 10% of capacity for two weeks with p99 prefill latency not regressing >5% and overall cost per token reduced.

Rollout & revert plan: 
- Feature gated and rollout via runtime-1.20 canary channels. Monitor slab_fallbacks, prefill_queue_length, memcpy_ops_per_request, and p99 latency.
- Revert is safe: allocator fallbacks to global allocator and hints are ignored by kernel router. Rollback toggle available in SRE console and via kill-switch env var.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: fragmentation of per-NUMA pools causing memory pressure. Mitigation: global eviction policy and configurable slab sizes; metric alert on slab_pressure.
- Risk: misclassification of token priority leading to suboptimal fusion. Mitigation: dynamic re-tagging of requests and conservative thresholds for short-path.
- Risk: kernel hint complexity adds maintenance surface. Mitigation: keep hints minimal and advisory; add feature flag for hint emission.

Observability: add dashboards for slab_hit_rate, memcpy_ops_histogram, prefill_queue_wait_ms separated by priority bucket, kernel_hint_adoption_rate, and end-to-end p99 latency by instance-type and socket-count.

Links: design doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/runtime/numa-io-fusion, perf harness: https://internal-reports.redwood/perf/834120, spike notes & microbench results: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/numa-spike-834120
comments: 2025-02-14: Spike complete — initial NUMA slab allocator prototype reduces allocation latency by ~18% on local allocations; cross-socket fallback penalty observed ~2.6x. — Miguel
2025-02-20: Design review with Runtime team. Agreed to make kernel hints advisory only. PM requested a clear rollout metric for customer-facing P99. Action: add detailed canary checklist. — Aisha
2025-02-27: IO fusion micro-batcher implemented and benchmarked in harness: memcpy ops per short request down from median 3 -> 1.5. Still need to validate under high concurrency. — Miguel
2025-03-03: Infra flagged potential memory pressure on instances with smaller RAM. Added slab size cap and eviction proto. Running extended perf runs. — SRE (Jordan Lee)
2025-03-05: Code PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/12987 (WIP). Requesting review from @cheng and @olivia for kernel selector integration. — Miguel
